subject: zoology_2
question_text: What is meant by genetic drift? Explain genetic drift citing the example of Founder Effect.

mark_split.label: Fixation or loss of an allele

verification.note: Sourced from 'My Baby Bullet-Q — Senior Inter Zoology' (Star-Q Pass Track Series, Sri Publishers, 2022), book p.41, SAQ 40. The printed exam years are the book's claim, reproduced here as appearances. steps.label: What genetic drift is
steps.why: In a small group, which individuals happen to breed can change gene frequencies without any advantage being involved.
common_mistakes: Calling drift a form of natural selection. It works by chance, not by selection.
Leaving out that it matters in SMALL populations.
steps.memory_tip: Drift is chance; selection is advantage.
steps.margin_note: Say 'by chance' and 'small populations'. Both are marked.
lines: Genetic drift is the change in the
frequency of a gene that occurs merely by
chance, and not by selection, in small
populations.

steps.label: Fixation or loss
steps.why: A rare allele can vanish simply because the few individuals carrying it did not happen to breed.
common_mistakes: Saying a rare allele always survives.
Leaving out that the outcome depends on population size.
steps.memory_tip: A rare allele in a small group either takes over or disappears.
steps.margin_note: Give the 1 per cent example. It makes the point concrete.
lines: A gene may have two alleles. If the
frequency of one allele is only 1%, the
chance of losing it from a small population
is high.
The end result is either fixation or loss
of that allele.
The chance of reaching either end point
depends on the size of the population.

steps.label: Its effect on variation
steps.why: Every allele lost is variation the population can never get back except by a new mutation.
common_mistakes: Saying drift increases variation. It reduces it.
Leaving out that it is the low-frequency alleles that go.
steps.memory_tip: Drift removes the rare alleles, so variation shrinks.
steps.margin_note: One line links drift to the founder effect.
lines: Genetic drift tends to reduce the amount of
genetic variation within a population,
mainly by removing the alleles with low
frequencies.
Genetic drift can be exemplified by the
founder effect.

steps.label: The founder effect
steps.why: The few individuals who start a new colony carry only a sample of the original variation, and their descendants inherit that sample.
common_mistakes: Saying the new colony resembles the parent population. It resembles its founders.
steps.memory_tip: The colony looks like its founders, not like the population they left.
steps.margin_note: Define it, then give the blood-group example.
lines: If a small group of individuals from a
population starts a new colony in an
isolated region, those individuals are
called the founders of the new population.
The allelic frequency of their descendants
is similar to that of the founders rather
than of the ancestral parent population.

lines.text: Example: O⁺ blood group is near 100% in some tribes

insider_note: The marking words are 'by chance and not by selection'. Drift is the opposite of natural selection, and saying so earns the first mark on its own.
